## 1. The partners and the one man  (`#the-shared-man`)

Cited ayat: 30:28, 39:29

> **30:28** ضَرَبَ لَكُم مَّثَلًا مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ هَل لَّكُم مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُم مِّن شُرَكَآءَ فِى مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ فَأَنتُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ تَخَافُونَهُمْ كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلْـَٔايَٰتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ

> **39:29** ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَّجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ مُتَشَٰكِسُونَ وَرَجُلًا سَلَمًا لِّرَجُلٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًا ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (30:28): God struck for them a similitude from themselves: do you have, among those you own, partners in what God provided for you, so that you are equal in it, fearing them as you fear one another? Thus God makes the signs clear for a people who use reason.

**c2** (39:29): God struck a similitude: a man in whom are quarrelling partners, and a man wholly for one man; the ayah asks whether they are equal in likeness.

**c3** (39:29): The ayah says that all praise is for God, but that most of them do not know.

### One-minute summary

One ayah gives a similitude from themselves and asks whether they have partners among those they own, equal with them in what God provided [c1]. Another gives a similitude of a man in whom are quarrelling partners and a man wholly for one man [c2].

### Complete story

God struck for them a similitude from themselves [c1]. It asks whether they have, among those they own, partners in what God provided for them, so that they are equal in it, fearing them as they fear one another [c1]. Thus God makes the signs clear for a people who use reason [c1].

In another ayah, God struck a similitude: a man in whom are quarrelling partners, and a man wholly for one man [c2]. The ayah asks whether they are equal in likeness [c2]. It says that all praise is for God, but that most of them do not know [c3].

### Deep study

Each similitude is built as a question the listeners can answer from their own life [c1][c2]. The first begins with the words from themselves, and the other contrasts one man belonging to quarrelling partners with one man belonging wholly to a single master [c1][c2]. The ayat are in different surahs, and they do not say whether they are one similitude or separate similitudes [c1][c2].

### Kids mode

God struck a similitude from themselves about partners among those they own [c1]. God also struck a similitude of a man in whom are quarrelling partners and a man wholly for one man [c2]. The ayah asks whether they are equal [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the first similitude asks whether anyone treats those they own as equal partners in what God provided [c1]. Another reading is that the later similitude sets a man pulled by quarrelling partners beside a man wholly for one man [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the people addressed are, or what the partners stand for; the ayat state the pictures as questions and give no key.
- Not established: whether the ayat are one similitude or separate similitudes.
- The ayat themselves use the word for a similitude (mathal) in both places.
- The Arabic of 30:28 speaks of those whom the right hands possess; this draft says 'those you own' and keeps the wording general.
